Source reference controls materials and identity. Second reference controls only the narrow vertical Y-footprint geometry; do not copy grey color. TOP-down plan of a Y-extended upright west wall. In these overhead/underside views, the full vertical finial or sconce front must be occluded, with only edge/foot footprints visible. No other objects, no labels, no text, no shadows, no perspective or isometric camera.

prompt: Generate one isolated transparent orthographic TOP-DOWN plan atlas with EXACTLY one column and two rows. Row 1 is the sand-coloured glass west wall; row 2 is the dark club panel west wall. The source contact controls each row's exact palette and identity. The second reference is a successful Y-wall top-plan geometry guide only; recolor geometry from each source. A top-down camera sees ONLY a narrow top cap rail and the tiny horizontal top faces of finial/support posts. The central vertical glass pane and the vertical illuminated sconce face are physically perpendicular to the camera and MUST be completely occluded. Do not draw their front colors, lamp, glass, wall face, three square panels, vertical finials, or any upright post silhouettes. Leave the center of the footprint dark/transparent, with only narrow rails along both long sides and small cap blocks at the two ends. Final plan is a thin vertical strip along world Y, 37×187 proportions. No perspective, text, labels, shadows or extra objects.
